items.excerpt: Take-a-Break's Fiction Feast magazine has told its regular contributors that 'AI tools will be used' on upcoming in-house stories, a notable shift in editorial practice for one of the UK's best-known short-fiction titles.

AI dominated the 35th International Publishers Association Congress in Kuala Lumpur, with IPA president Gvantsa Jobava stressing that 'our books are valuable individually and collectively' as training data and the industry moving from fascination to practical implementation questions.

Publishers and author Scott Turow filed what Book Riot calls the most straightforward case yet against a tech company's use of books to train AI, alleging Google used titles from its Scholar, Books, and Play Store platforms outside their agreed uses.
A copyright lawsuit filed in New York names Hachette, Cengage, and Elsevier, plus author Scott Turow, alleging Google unlawfully used copyrighted books to train its Gemini AI models.

Audiobook publisher Bolinda used interviews, archival research and human input to build an AI clone of the late romance novelist Barbara Cartland's voice, using it to narrate her catalogue and revive a distinctive authorial voice for new audiobook editions.
